reason: Reads the address without Next's useSearchParams, which the release's hook still reads in 0.15.0. Reading search params client-renders every Client Component up to the nearest Suspense boundary, which costs three pages their prerender: restoring Meridian's own text on 2026-10-12 put /teams at LCP 0.63 s -> 2.27 s, /people 0.64 -> 2.16 and /activity 0.64 -> 2.08 on the phone profile, and scripts/route-policy.ts reported `2 static, 22 partial, 0 dynamic` for BOTH builds, so it cannot see the difference. Rebuilding a write from window.location rather than from Next's copy was the other half of this entry, and 0.15.0 does that itself. Reading the address here owes two things the release's hook does not: the readers are told once the navigation has committed, and a write stays shown until they are told. The transition settles one render before that, and a search box kept with the release's useSearchDraft took the address as it was before the write for a change from elsewhere: on /teams a key typed up to 40 ms after the box's own write was lost in 15 of 24 trials, and in 0 of 24 with the write held (2026-10-14). Reported upstream as zz-meridian#22; this entry comes out when Meridian reads the address itself.

A stream opened by a page that has just read its own data does not resync: resyncing there read a document body three times and put the largest paint at 2,676 ms against a 2,500 ms bar, measured on a document route at 390 px under the phone profile. A stream that follows being away still resyncs. Reported upstream as zz-meridian#23; this entry comes out when the release tells the two apart.

The product's own period vocabulary, which this file's own comment says a product edits here so the picker follows: a 24-hour period, all time as the default (a console that opens on 30 days shows a total that is not the total), and `periodCutoff`. Meridian manages the file and also directs a product to edit it; reported upstream as zz-meridian#24.
